title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
claim: Human choice data is turned into embeddings, then dimensions are pruned one at a time to rank which drives a decision.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, nested loop box with Repeat×n
description: The figure has two stacked panels split by a dashed line. Panel (a) runs left to right. A THINGS database image mosaic (1854 objects) goes through a crowd-sourcing icon to an odd-one-out triplet of photos (mousetrap, matchbox, aardvark) with a pointing hand. A SPoSE icon then produces three colored embedding rows (green i, black j, red k) over n dimensions. Panel (b), labeled Dimension Jackknife, sits in a rounded Repeat×n box. Embeddings go through softmax to choice probabilities (0.8, 0.1, 0.1). One dimension is cut out with scissors and softmax is run again (0.3, 0.6, 0.1). The probability difference is stored in a tall mauve relevance bar, then sorted into a light-blue list of named dimensions such as metallic, food-related and animal-related. Bold labels and arrows guide the eye.
caption: Overview of triplet-level semantic dimension attribution. (a) Human similarity judgements are collected via crowdsourcing. Then learning a representational embedding space via SPoSE yields the multidimensional mental representations of natural objects. (b) For one triplet, we compute the original softmax probability based on the entire representational embedding for all pairs. We then iteratively prune each dimension from the representational embedding space and compute the changes in softmax probabilities relative to those obtained with the full embedding as the relevance score for that dimension. By sorting these relevance scores in descending order, we establish a hierarchical ranking of dimensional importance. The top-1 dimension yielding the maximum probability change is regarded as the most salient semantic dimension driving the human decision-making.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations and decision criteria align with the latent structure of human cognition. In this work, we propose a novel framework to align MLLMs with the multidimensional mental representations underlying human similarity judgements. We build on a previously established behavior-derived semantic embedding space, in which objects are represented along 66 interpretable dimensions derived from 4.70 million human Odd-One-Out (O1O) judgements. For each triplet, we infer the most salient decision dimension and convert it into a dimension-grounded linguistic rationale. This enables MLLMs to learn both the final choice and a justification consistent with the inferred behavioral criterion. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves model consistency with human similarity judgements while retaining competitive performance on standard multimodal benchmarks. Furthermore, using searchlight Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) on an independent fMRI Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we observe increased representational alignment between model and human. Ultimately, our findings point to a data-driven route for incorporating human cognitive structure into MLLMs alignment. The code is available \href{https://github.com/ening-open/cogalign}{here}.
